scope: Paper-v1 research source release: bounded software execution checks, frozen paper references, separately acquired assets/data/weights.

skip_reasons: One USD test requires pxr; executed successfully on Linux

checks: Actual PhysX GPU and IsaacRtxRenderer startup
Two nonuniform 224x224 RGB camera views, before and after stepping
Task-specific outcome collection; hold success values are not policy scores

isaaclab_source_identity.source_hash_recipe: SHA256(JSON of sorted POSIX relative path and file SHA256 pairs; .py/.toml/VERSION, excluding caches and venvs)

environment.native_environment_repair: Matching environment libstdc++.so.6 selected by LD_PRELOAD; libXt/libSM/libICE supplied by an isolated native-library directory. No global system libraries were replaced.

official_package.explanation: 6.1.14 is the original editable core extension metadata, not the public isaaclab distribution version. The wheel bundles the sub-packages.

difference_interpretation: All 429 core isaaclab Python files and all 20 isaaclab_rl Python files match byte-for-byte.
Four sub-package __init__.py files adjust metadata directory lookup for the wheel layout; numerical definitions are unchanged in those files.
The original editable Factory environment has two additional optional pi05 camera patches. Those environment modules were not imported in these ten ForceBench checks.
The official wheel adds its distribution bootstrap and nested core-module layout; module-origin checks and actual GPU execution test that packaged layout.

gpu_validation.environment_installation: Official wheel extracted into a new directory and selected by PYTHONPATH; all other simulator dependencies inherited from the existing environment.

limitations: Bounded hold-action simulator checks, not task-success scores, full model training or paper-result reproduction.
This is not a fresh dependency installation; it validates the official wheel over existing compatible simulator dependencies.
The original editable Git revision remains unknown. The public wheel hash is a separate reproducible artifact identity.
Factory/FORGE agent metadata namespaces may be registered by startup; their environment implementations and optional camera patch modules were not loaded.
An earlier GPU4 remapped diagnostic was aborted and excluded because its CUDA/Kit device mapping was not accepted as reliable.

subsequent_launcher_checks.scope: CPU routing tests; simulator execution above uses the same direct-Python numerical scripts.

websocket.handler: Native ForceFlow server and forceflow_ws adapter

environment.base_parameter_loading: Real pi0_base or pi05_base parameters; no fake model

input_scope.use: Actual decoded images/states/actions/wrench batches and recorded inference observations for the nine OpenPI systems; not all trajectories were evaluated.
ForceFlow real data, full normalizer-boundary comparison, short training and inference.

transport_exception.reason: GitHub Git fetch failed over HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1 TLS; an initial offline attempt also lacked a cached JAX wheel.

fresh_install_check.scope: Controlled pi05 environment and F4 only; not a fresh installation of all baseline variants.

representative_simulator_model_closed_lo.model: Real pi05_base plus explicit Faucet normalization; zero task-training updates
representative_simulator_model_closed_lo.pipeline: Actual simulator RGB/state -> openpi_ws adapter -> GPU model inference -> absolute TCP actions -> simulator controller
representative_simulator_model_closed_lo.scope: One environment and eight executed steps from a real model-generated 50-action chunk. This verifies an action pipeline, not complete-task success, a trained checkpoint or a benchmark score.

limitations: Software execution validation only; no task-success estimates or paper-result reproduction were produced.
Nine OpenPI systems ran three updates at preserved global batch sizes with diagnostic num_workers=0. No production 10000-update checkpoint save/restore was tested for them.
Loopback OpenPI handler tests do not validate ForceVLA production single/batched server modes or their batching equivalence.

Explicit data and normalization inputs are not proof of final historical paper checkpoint, data and normalization mapping. The pi0 diagnostic used the explicit compatible state/action norm asset selected for the software check, not a verified historical pi0 norm.
Full dataset/base-weight payload checksum audits, all task-method cells, convergence, statistical repeatability and real-world operation are outside this check.
ForceFlow used an existing environment and a small batch for its two-step diagnostic. Its native CLI was also exercised for two steps; neither is a full training run.
Production checkpoint identity/budget gates were preserved; no identity bypass or fabricated receipt was used.

expert_collection.gpu_startup: 32 environments, actual RTX reset/initial recording checked; hard-timeout stopped
expert_collection.stove_press_quality_timepoint: Per-clone post-action completion snapshot for both retained trajectory and quality gates; thresholds/physics preserved

scoring_changes: Stove geometry test uses actual compact burner center; runtime SPEC position unchanged
Faucet Direction new-run paper scorer uses signed final angle >= resistance peak, with no upper bound; historical band scorer retained explicitly
Historical batch-end state is separate from first simultaneous success and fixed post-success stability
limitations: This is not reproduction of the 80 simulation task-method scores, convergence or statistical repeatability.
Original paper checkpoint-to-data-to-normalizer bindings remain incomplete; frozen table values are not overwritten by new runs.

The historical Isaac Lab Git commit remains unknown. The official 3.0.0b2.post1 wheel is source-compared and GPU-executed as a public installation target; its remaining dependencies were inherited, so a complete fresh simulator installation is unverified.

Exact external meshes, textures, datasets and weights must be obtained separately under their applicable terms; current asset import pins identity rather than granting rights or providing public downloads.
The recovered expert collectors were initialized/rendered, not run to complete the 1600 demonstrations.
Real-world reference values do not constitute a validated real-robot deployment.

ci.skip_reason: pxr not installed in lightweight CPU runner; covered by H200 CPU suite
ci.scope: Clean CPU install before the final launcher-only additions; the current commit is checked again by CI.
